rule_sets.name: Year 2 alternative pathway
rule_sets.notes: This degree focuses on Applied Computing, which is fundamentally related to applying computing technology and computational methods to derive solutions to complex practical problems. Course work will emphasize current issues in industry, case studies, and applied research projects. This program offers you a chance to work with an interdisciplinary and diverse team of academic supervisors that may include faculty from Computing, faculty from an application domain, as well as industry practitioners. You’ll also have the opportunity to undertake directed studies with a supervisor in a different department to explore a specific application area. For more information about faculty, visit the Faculty, Advisors & Staff page. Applied research is fundamental to the program. Two paths are offered, diverging in second year: Thesis Path – Path 1: complete a thesis project and defend it in your second year. You’ll need to demonstrate originality in the application of your knowledge, either through new publishable research, or a novel solution to an existing practical problem. This is the best path if you’re interested in possibly pursuing a future Ph.D. Project & Internship Path – Path 2: a one-semester research project with a one-semester internship, which may be paid or unpaid. The internship will involve an external company or a BCIT lab where you can learn how advanced computing techniques are applied to solve interdisciplinary problems. The research project may be done in collaboration with the sponsor from the internship, providing added value in terms of practical utility. Students will also complete a 3-credit special topics course, covering emerging areas in Applied Computing, such as Quantum Computing, Generative AI, or Deep Learning. Both paths will require students to: examine literature in a related discipline, recognize gaps and limitations in existing technologies and processes, organize and plan their approach, and demonstrate competence in applying advanced techniques to solve problems. In both paths, students will present a written argument that addresses a complex problem in applied computing. Did you miss our Info Session? Please see the recording from October 2024: BCIT Master of Science in Applied Computing | Info Session Program length Two years, full-time. The maximum time to complete this program is five years. Grading Students will be required to maintain a minimum average of 70% across all courses in the program before starting their thesis or research project. Student progress through the program will be monitored by the supervisor, in consultation with the Program Head. Program delivery In person: This program is delivered on campus. Program location Burnaby Campus 3700 Willingdon Avenue Burnaby, BC Go back Courses Next up Graduating & Jobs

program.program_overview: The Master of Science Degree in Applied Computing gives you in-depth computing knowledge to solve complex real-world problems across industries and sectors. Through an interdisciplinary and rigorous full-time curriculum, you’ll be equipped to provide technical leadership in a professional setting or pursue further academic study. Note: The September 2026 intake is now closed for new applications. Applications for the September 2027 intake will be accepted starting October 1, 2026. Delivery: in person. See details . BCIT Master of Science in Applied Computing About the program Applied computing integrates information technology, computer science, and industry. You’ll take courses in core computing, and you will have the opportunity to work in an application area in another discipline. You’ll develop a deep understanding of how advanced computing, tools, and computational methods can be applied in practice to overcome challenges and create efficiencies. The program employs a cohort model, with the same group in all courses. This allows you to work through the program together, sharing your experience and expertise and building industry connections that will last long after you graduate 1 intake: September 4 15-week terms, normally completed over two academic years full time First year with two terms , delivered in-person, including: Algorithm analysis Human-centered Computing Machine Learning (ML) & Artificial Intelligence (AI) Data Science Cybersecurity Research methods Second year on thesis path or internship & project path Based on BCIT Burnaby Campus, and possibly the Downtown Campus or field locations where appropriate. You’ll be uniquely qualified to apply your knowledge and skills in various areas, such as: computational science rehabilitation engineering building science biotechnology autonomous vehicles sustainability smart micro-grids social impacts of technology network security an approved project area of your choosing based on your professional background See the Program Details to learn more. Who it’s for This degree might be for you if you: Are inspired to maximize the societal benefit of computing by solving real-world issues Would like to apply your skills in industry after graduation, but might also consider applying for a PhD Are looking for a cohort-based program where you’ll work with other students to share problem-solving skills and approaches, as you would in a work setting Have an applied problem you believe could be improved through computing Would like to study with computing faculty, application experts outside of computing, and industry partners Students will also have the opportunity to undertake directed studies with a supervisor in a different department to gain additional knowledge in a specific application area. Please review the Entrance Requirements to learn more. What grads can do Provide technical leadership for software/system development teams Demonstrate deep, critical knowledge and understanding of advanced topics in computing science Analyze how computing systems and software can be used in practical applications and interdisciplinary fields Design, develop, and implement innovative solutions to industry problems with consideration to relevant ethical, social and environmental issues Explain and advocate for applied computing solutions to specialist and non-specialist audiences in both business and academic settings See the Graduating & Jobs page to learn more. Next up Entrance Requirements

conversation.content: What should I know before applying?

Before applying to the **Applied Computing — Master of Science**, know the following:

### Intake and application timing
- The **September 2026 intake is closed**.
- Applications for **September 2027** are scheduled to open **October 1, 2026**.
- The listed application rounds are:
  - **October 1–January 31**
  - **February 1–March 31**
  - **April 1–June 15**
  - Dates may move to the next business day.
- International applicants need a valid **BCIT study permit** to apply in the third round.

### Entrance requirements
You must meet the English requirement and **one** of the following entry routes:

- **English:** Graduate Studies English Studies 12 with at least **67%**, or an equivalent qualification.
- **Standard entry:** A bachelor’s degree in computer science or an equivalent field, with at least **2.8/4.0 (70%)** across the final 30 undergraduate credits.
- **Alternate entry:** A bachelor’s degree in another discipline, with at least **3.0/4.0 (73%)** across the final 30 credits, plus significant computing knowledge through education and/or work experience. You must also complete a **Pre-entry Assessment**; bridging courses may be required before applying.

### Application materials and selection
Prepare to:

- Submit proof that you meet the entrance requirements.
- Complete the **Mandatory Applicant Questionnaire**.
- Provide **two references**. Referees must email their reference forms directly to the M.Sc. admissions committee, up to one week after the deadline.
- If your post-secondary studies were completed outside Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, or New Zealand, obtain a comprehensive **International Credential Evaluation Service (ICES)** evaluation. Other Canadian evaluation services may be considered.
- Convert transcripts and supporting documents to PDF.
- Have a credit card available for the application fee.

Admission is competitive: complete applications are reviewed and ranked by the Graduate Program Committee. Relevant industry experience is preferred but is **not listed as a minimum requirement**. Applicants currently completing their degree must be on track to graduate by July before the program starts.

### Other points to consider
- The program is **full-time and in person**, normally completed over two academic years.
- In Year 2, you choose **one** path:
  - Thesis Path: **COMP 9600 — M.Sc. Thesis**
  - Project & Internship Path: **COMP 9290 — Special Topics in Applied Computing**, **COMP 9400 — Industry Internship**, and **COMP 9500 — M.Sc. Research Project**
- You must maintain at least a **70% average across program courses before starting the thesis or research project**.
- International students must obtain a valid BCIT study permit before starting. The program is identified as eligible for graduates to apply for a post-graduation work permit, but final approval depends on meeting IRCC requirements.

Because no personal academic or English-language details were provided, I cannot determine which entry route you personally meet. Requirements involving references, credential evaluation, and competitive departmental review require confirmation by the institution.

[View the program details and application information](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/applied-computing-master-of-science-full-time-m600msc/)

- If your post-secondary studies were completed outside Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, or New Zealand, you need a comprehensive **International Credential Evaluation Service (ICES)** evaluation. Other Canadian evaluation services may be considered.
- You must meet the English requirement and one entry route:
  - A computer science or equivalent bachelor’s degree with at least **2.8/4.0 (70%)** over your final 30 undergraduate credits; or
  - A bachelor’s degree in another discipline with at least **3.0/4.0 (73%)**, plus significant computing knowledge and completion of the required pre-entry assessment.
- Admission is competitive. You must also submit the **Mandatory Applicant Questionnaire** and **two references** sent directly to the admissions committee.
- The program currently meets the study-program requirements for graduates to apply for a **post-graduation work permit (PGWP)**. Final approval depends on meeting all **IRCC** requirements.
- The September 2026 intake is closed. Applications for September 2027 are scheduled to open **October 1, 2026**.

rule_sets.name: Applied Computing MSc competitive admission
rule_sets.notes: Applicants currently in the final term of their degree program must be on track to graduate by July prior to the start of the intake and may be conditionally accepted based on successful completion of their degree. Scheduled intakes September each year. Application processing Applications are accepted: First round: October 1st* to January 31st* Second round: February 1st* to March 31st* Third round: April 1st* to June 15th* International applicants must hold a valid BCIT study permit to apply to the third round. *or next business day Indigenous applicants: Read about Indigenous student support available for BCIT Computing programs. Entrance requirements Competitive entry: Two-step process Admission to the program is competitive, with preference given to applicants with a combination of: Academic grades above the minimum Relevant industry experience Step 1: Meet the following entrance requirements: English language proficiency: Graduate Studies – English Studies 12 (67%) or equivalent One of the following entry requirements: Option 1: standard entry Post-secondary education: A bachelor’s degree in computer science or equivalent, such as BCIT’s Bachelor of Science in Applied Computer Science , with a minimum GPA of 2.8 out of 4.0 (70%) based on the final 30 credits of undergraduate study at BCIT or equivalent (e.g., one year of full-time studies). Option 2: alternate entry Alternate entry is for applicants who don’t have a bachelor's degree in computer science and may need to take bridging courses before being accepted to the program. Applicants are required to have the following: Post-secondary education: bachelor's degree with a minimum GPA of 3.0 out of 4.0 (73%) in another discipline based on the final 30 credits of undergraduate study, with significant knowledge of computing through formal education and/or work experience. Completed Pre-entry Assessment form [PDF] : submit the form to CompMSc@bcit.ca . The program area will review your pre-entry assessment and bridging courses may be required before applying to the program. Bridging courses will be recommended from existing COMP courses at BCIT, although transferable course work from other recognized Canadian post-secondary institutions may also be used. Applicants may be requested to send additional documents or meet with the program area. Complete the following form for submission with your online application: Mandatory Applicant Questionnaire [PDF] : This form will be used with other entrance requirements in the competitive selection for the program. Please note that two references are required on the form, and that the people listed as references must directly email their reference form to the M.Sc. admissions committee up to one week after the application deadline. Applicants who have completed post-secondary studies outside of Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia or New Zealand will require a comprehensive evaluation of their credentials by the International Credential Evaluation Service (ICES) . Credential evaluation reports from other Canadian services may be considered. Step 2: Department Review All complete applications will be reviewed by the Graduate Program Committee and ranked competitively, and applicants will be offered admission accordingly. Only complete applications with all the required supporting documentation will be evaluated for admission consideration to the program. Recommended for success Applicants with a sufficient knowledge base in computer science will be best positioned for success in this program. This may include students who have studied information and communications technology (ICT), engineering, physics, mathematics, applied sciences, or other areas where they have been exposed to computing, information technology, and programming concepts. International applicants This program is available to international applicants. Study permit: A valid BCIT study permit is required prior to starting the program. Students enrolled in the Project & Internship Path of this program must complete the mandatory work component to qualify for graduation. Post-graduation Work Permit (PGWP) eligibility : This program currently meets the PGWP eligibility requirements based on study program - graduates with a master's degree and is eligible for students to apply for a PGWP. There are no field of study requirements (CIP) for graduates with a master’s degree. Students are responsible for meeting all Immigration, Refugees, and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) PGWP eligibility requirements . Final PGWP approval is at the discretion of IRCC. Apply to program Note: The September 2026 intake is now closed for new applications. Applications for the September 2027 intake will be accepted starting October 1, 2026. To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply Go back Overview Next up Costs & Supplies

rule_sets.name: Year 2 alternative pathway
rule_sets.notes: This degree focuses on Applied Computing, which is fundamentally related to applying computing technology and computational methods to derive solutions to complex practical problems. Course work will emphasize current issues in industry, case studies, and applied research projects. This program offers you a chance to work with an interdisciplinary and diverse team of academic supervisors that may include faculty from Computing, faculty from an application domain, as well as industry practitioners. You’ll also have the opportunity to undertake directed studies with a supervisor in a different department to explore a specific application area. For more information about faculty, visit the Faculty, Advisors & Staff page. Applied research is fundamental to the program. Two paths are offered, diverging in second year: Thesis Path – Path 1: complete a thesis project and defend it in your second year. You’ll need to demonstrate originality in the application of your knowledge, either through new publishable research, or a novel solution to an existing practical problem. This is the best path if you’re interested in possibly pursuing a future Ph.D. Project & Internship Path – Path 2: a one-semester research project with a one-semester internship, which may be paid or unpaid. The internship will involve an external company or a BCIT lab where you can learn how advanced computing techniques are applied to solve interdisciplinary problems. The research project may be done in collaboration with the sponsor from the internship, providing added value in terms of practical utility. Students will also complete a 3-credit special topics course, covering emerging areas in Applied Computing, such as Quantum Computing, Generative AI, or Deep Learning. Both paths will require students to: examine literature in a related discipline, recognize gaps and limitations in existing technologies and processes, organize and plan their approach, and demonstrate competence in applying advanced techniques to solve problems. In both paths, students will present a written argument that addresses a complex problem in applied computing. Did you miss our Info Session? Please see the recording from October 2024: BCIT Master of Science in Applied Computing | Info Session Program length Two years, full-time. The maximum time to complete this program is five years. Grading Students will be required to maintain a minimum average of 70% across all courses in the program before starting their thesis or research project. Student progress through the program will be monitored by the supervisor, in consultation with the Program Head. Program delivery In person: This program is delivered on campus. Program location Burnaby Campus 3700 Willingdon Avenue Burnaby, BC Go back Courses Next up Graduating & Jobs

program.program_overview: The Master of Science Degree in Applied Computing gives you in-depth computing knowledge to solve complex real-world problems across industries and sectors. Through an interdisciplinary and rigorous full-time curriculum, you’ll be equipped to provide technical leadership in a professional setting or pursue further academic study. Note: The September 2026 intake is now closed for new applications. Applications for the September 2027 intake will be accepted starting October 1, 2026. Delivery: in person. See details . BCIT Master of Science in Applied Computing About the program Applied computing integrates information technology, computer science, and industry. You’ll take courses in core computing, and you will have the opportunity to work in an application area in another discipline. You’ll develop a deep understanding of how advanced computing, tools, and computational methods can be applied in practice to overcome challenges and create efficiencies. The program employs a cohort model, with the same group in all courses. This allows you to work through the program together, sharing your experience and expertise and building industry connections that will last long after you graduate 1 intake: September 4 15-week terms, normally completed over two academic years full time First year with two terms , delivered in-person, including: Algorithm analysis Human-centered Computing Machine Learning (ML) & Artificial Intelligence (AI) Data Science Cybersecurity Research methods Second year on thesis path or internship & project path Based on BCIT Burnaby Campus, and possibly the Downtown Campus or field locations where appropriate. You’ll be uniquely qualified to apply your knowledge and skills in various areas, such as: computational science rehabilitation engineering building science biotechnology autonomous vehicles sustainability smart micro-grids social impacts of technology network security an approved project area of your choosing based on your professional background See the Program Details to learn more. Who it’s for This degree might be for you if you: Are inspired to maximize the societal benefit of computing by solving real-world issues Would like to apply your skills in industry after graduation, but might also consider applying for a PhD Are looking for a cohort-based program where you’ll work with other students to share problem-solving skills and approaches, as you would in a work setting Have an applied problem you believe could be improved through computing Would like to study with computing faculty, application experts outside of computing, and industry partners Students will also have the opportunity to undertake directed studies with a supervisor in a different department to gain additional knowledge in a specific application area. Please review the Entrance Requirements to learn more. What grads can do Provide technical leadership for software/system development teams Demonstrate deep, critical knowledge and understanding of advanced topics in computing science Analyze how computing systems and software can be used in practical applications and interdisciplinary fields Design, develop, and implement innovative solutions to industry problems with consideration to relevant ethical, social and environmental issues Explain and advocate for applied computing solutions to specialist and non-specialist audiences in both business and academic settings See the Graduating & Jobs page to learn more. Next up Entrance Requirements

conversation.content: Does that guarantee admission?

No. Meeting the entrance requirements does **not guarantee admission** to the Applied Computing Master of Science.

Admission is competitive: complete applications are reviewed and ranked by the Graduate Program Committee, and offers are made accordingly. You must also submit the required questionnaire and references; international applicants may need a comprehensive ICES evaluation, depending on where their prior studies were completed.

For international applicants, a valid BCIT study permit is required before starting the program. The September 2026 intake is closed; applications for September 2027 are scheduled to open October 1, 2026.

[View the program and application details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/applied-computing-master-of-science-full-time-m600msc/)

For more information, see BCIT Admissions: https://www.bcit.ca/admission/.
Which details need human confirmation?

For the **Applied Computing — Master of Science**, these details require confirmation by BCIT, the program area, or the relevant authority:

- **English equivalency:** Whether your English credential is equivalent to **English Studies 12 with at least 67%**.
- **Alternate-entry eligibility:** Whether your computing knowledge is sufficient if your bachelor’s degree is in another discipline, and whether bridging courses or additional documents are required.
- **Applicant Questionnaire:** Confirmation that the submitted **Mandatory Applicant Questionnaire** is complete and acceptable.
- **References:** Confirmation that **two references** have been submitted directly to the admissions committee in the required format and timeframe.
- **International credential evaluation:** If your studies were completed outside Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, or New Zealand, confirmation that a comprehensive **ICES evaluation** is required and whether another Canadian evaluation service will be accepted.
- **Competitive review:** The Graduate Program Committee’s assessment and ranking of your complete application. Meeting the stated minimums does **not** guarantee admission.
- **Relevant industry experience:** It is preferred, but the record does not specify how the committee evaluates it.
- **Study permit:** International students must confirm current study-permit requirements with BCIT and the applicable immigration authorities before starting.
- **PGWP:** The program is identified as eligible for graduates to apply, but final approval depends on meeting all **IRCC** requirements.

The program’s verified details and application link are available here:  
https://www.bcit.ca/programs/applied-computing-master-of-science-full-time-m600msc/
Can you put that more simply?

Simply put, **meeting the minimum requirements does not guarantee admission**.

BCIT would still need to confirm:

- Whether your English qualification is equivalent to **English Studies 12 with 67%**.
- If you use the alternate entry route, whether your computing experience is sufficient and whether bridging courses are needed.
- Whether your questionnaire and two references are complete and acceptable.
- Whether you need an **ICES credential evaluation**.
- Whether your complete application is ranked high enough in the competitive review.
- For international students, your study-permit requirements.
- Whether you personally meet all **IRCC requirements** for a post-graduation work permit.

The final admission decision is made through BCIT’s competitive review process.

[Program and application details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/applied-computing-master-of-science-full-time-m600msc/)

rule_sets.name: Applied Computing MSc competitive admission
rule_sets.notes: Applicants currently in the final term of their degree program must be on track to graduate by July prior to the start of the intake and may be conditionally accepted based on successful completion of their degree. Scheduled intakes September each year. Application processing Applications are accepted: First round: October 1st* to January 31st* Second round: February 1st* to March 31st* Third round: April 1st* to June 15th* International applicants must hold a valid BCIT study permit to apply to the third round. *or next business day Indigenous applicants: Read about Indigenous student support available for BCIT Computing programs. Entrance requirements Competitive entry: Two-step process Admission to the program is competitive, with preference given to applicants with a combination of: Academic grades above the minimum Relevant industry experience Step 1: Meet the following entrance requirements: English language proficiency: Graduate Studies – English Studies 12 (67%) or equivalent One of the following entry requirements: Option 1: standard entry Post-secondary education: A bachelor’s degree in computer science or equivalent, such as BCIT’s Bachelor of Science in Applied Computer Science , with a minimum GPA of 2.8 out of 4.0 (70%) based on the final 30 credits of undergraduate study at BCIT or equivalent (e.g., one year of full-time studies). Option 2: alternate entry Alternate entry is for applicants who don’t have a bachelor's degree in computer science and may need to take bridging courses before being accepted to the program. Applicants are required to have the following: Post-secondary education: bachelor's degree with a minimum GPA of 3.0 out of 4.0 (73%) in another discipline based on the final 30 credits of undergraduate study, with significant knowledge of computing through formal education and/or work experience. Completed Pre-entry Assessment form [PDF] : submit the form to CompMSc@bcit.ca . The program area will review your pre-entry assessment and bridging courses may be required before applying to the program. Bridging courses will be recommended from existing COMP courses at BCIT, although transferable course work from other recognized Canadian post-secondary institutions may also be used. Applicants may be requested to send additional documents or meet with the program area. Complete the following form for submission with your online application: Mandatory Applicant Questionnaire [PDF] : This form will be used with other entrance requirements in the competitive selection for the program. Please note that two references are required on the form, and that the people listed as references must directly email their reference form to the M.Sc. admissions committee up to one week after the application deadline. Applicants who have completed post-secondary studies outside of Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia or New Zealand will require a comprehensive evaluation of their credentials by the International Credential Evaluation Service (ICES) . Credential evaluation reports from other Canadian services may be considered. Step 2: Department Review All complete applications will be reviewed by the Graduate Program Committee and ranked competitively, and applicants will be offered admission accordingly. Only complete applications with all the required supporting documentation will be evaluated for admission consideration to the program. Recommended for success Applicants with a sufficient knowledge base in computer science will be best positioned for success in this program. This may include students who have studied information and communications technology (ICT), engineering, physics, mathematics, applied sciences, or other areas where they have been exposed to computing, information technology, and programming concepts. International applicants This program is available to international applicants. Study permit: A valid BCIT study permit is required prior to starting the program. Students enrolled in the Project & Internship Path of this program must complete the mandatory work component to qualify for graduation. Post-graduation Work Permit (PGWP) eligibility : This program currently meets the PGWP eligibility requirements based on study program - graduates with a master's degree and is eligible for students to apply for a PGWP. There are no field of study requirements (CIP) for graduates with a master’s degree. Students are responsible for meeting all Immigration, Refugees, and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) PGWP eligibility requirements . Final PGWP approval is at the discretion of IRCC. Apply to program Note: The September 2026 intake is now closed for new applications. Applications for the September 2027 intake will be accepted starting October 1, 2026. To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply Go back Overview Next up Costs & Supplies

rule_sets.name: Year 2 alternative pathway
rule_sets.notes: This degree focuses on Applied Computing, which is fundamentally related to applying computing technology and computational methods to derive solutions to complex practical problems. Course work will emphasize current issues in industry, case studies, and applied research projects. This program offers you a chance to work with an interdisciplinary and diverse team of academic supervisors that may include faculty from Computing, faculty from an application domain, as well as industry practitioners. You’ll also have the opportunity to undertake directed studies with a supervisor in a different department to explore a specific application area. For more information about faculty, visit the Faculty, Advisors & Staff page. Applied research is fundamental to the program. Two paths are offered, diverging in second year: Thesis Path – Path 1: complete a thesis project and defend it in your second year. You’ll need to demonstrate originality in the application of your knowledge, either through new publishable research, or a novel solution to an existing practical problem. This is the best path if you’re interested in possibly pursuing a future Ph.D. Project & Internship Path – Path 2: a one-semester research project with a one-semester internship, which may be paid or unpaid. The internship will involve an external company or a BCIT lab where you can learn how advanced computing techniques are applied to solve interdisciplinary problems. The research project may be done in collaboration with the sponsor from the internship, providing added value in terms of practical utility. Students will also complete a 3-credit special topics course, covering emerging areas in Applied Computing, such as Quantum Computing, Generative AI, or Deep Learning. Both paths will require students to: examine literature in a related discipline, recognize gaps and limitations in existing technologies and processes, organize and plan their approach, and demonstrate competence in applying advanced techniques to solve problems. In both paths, students will present a written argument that addresses a complex problem in applied computing. Did you miss our Info Session? Please see the recording from October 2024: BCIT Master of Science in Applied Computing | Info Session Program length Two years, full-time. The maximum time to complete this program is five years. Grading Students will be required to maintain a minimum average of 70% across all courses in the program before starting their thesis or research project. Student progress through the program will be monitored by the supervisor, in consultation with the Program Head. Program delivery In person: This program is delivered on campus. Program location Burnaby Campus 3700 Willingdon Avenue Burnaby, BC Go back Courses Next up Graduating & Jobs

program.program_overview: The Master of Science Degree in Applied Computing gives you in-depth computing knowledge to solve complex real-world problems across industries and sectors. Through an interdisciplinary and rigorous full-time curriculum, you’ll be equipped to provide technical leadership in a professional setting or pursue further academic study. Note: The September 2026 intake is now closed for new applications. Applications for the September 2027 intake will be accepted starting October 1, 2026. Delivery: in person. See details . BCIT Master of Science in Applied Computing About the program Applied computing integrates information technology, computer science, and industry. You’ll take courses in core computing, and you will have the opportunity to work in an application area in another discipline. You’ll develop a deep understanding of how advanced computing, tools, and computational methods can be applied in practice to overcome challenges and create efficiencies. The program employs a cohort model, with the same group in all courses. This allows you to work through the program together, sharing your experience and expertise and building industry connections that will last long after you graduate 1 intake: September 4 15-week terms, normally completed over two academic years full time First year with two terms , delivered in-person, including: Algorithm analysis Human-centered Computing Machine Learning (ML) & Artificial Intelligence (AI) Data Science Cybersecurity Research methods Second year on thesis path or internship & project path Based on BCIT Burnaby Campus, and possibly the Downtown Campus or field locations where appropriate. You’ll be uniquely qualified to apply your knowledge and skills in various areas, such as: computational science rehabilitation engineering building science biotechnology autonomous vehicles sustainability smart micro-grids social impacts of technology network security an approved project area of your choosing based on your professional background See the Program Details to learn more. Who it’s for This degree might be for you if you: Are inspired to maximize the societal benefit of computing by solving real-world issues Would like to apply your skills in industry after graduation, but might also consider applying for a PhD Are looking for a cohort-based program where you’ll work with other students to share problem-solving skills and approaches, as you would in a work setting Have an applied problem you believe could be improved through computing Would like to study with computing faculty, application experts outside of computing, and industry partners Students will also have the opportunity to undertake directed studies with a supervisor in a different department to gain additional knowledge in a specific application area. Please review the Entrance Requirements to learn more. What grads can do Provide technical leadership for software/system development teams Demonstrate deep, critical knowledge and understanding of advanced topics in computing science Analyze how computing systems and software can be used in practical applications and interdisciplinary fields Design, develop, and implement innovative solutions to industry problems with consideration to relevant ethical, social and environmental issues Explain and advocate for applied computing solutions to specialist and non-specialist audiences in both business and academic settings See the Graduating & Jobs page to learn more. Next up Entrance Requirements

rule_sets.name: Applied Computing MSc competitive admission
rule_sets.notes: Applicants currently in the final term of their degree program must be on track to graduate by July prior to the start of the intake and may be conditionally accepted based on successful completion of their degree. Scheduled intakes September each year. Application processing Applications are accepted: First round: October 1st* to January 31st* Second round: February 1st* to March 31st* Third round: April 1st* to June 15th* International applicants must hold a valid BCIT study permit to apply to the third round. *or next business day Indigenous applicants: Read about Indigenous student support available for BCIT Computing programs. Entrance requirements Competitive entry: Two-step process Admission to the program is competitive, with preference given to applicants with a combination of: Academic grades above the minimum Relevant industry experience Step 1: Meet the following entrance requirements: English language proficiency: Graduate Studies – English Studies 12 (67%) or equivalent One of the following entry requirements: Option 1: standard entry Post-secondary education: A bachelor’s degree in computer science or equivalent, such as BCIT’s Bachelor of Science in Applied Computer Science , with a minimum GPA of 2.8 out of 4.0 (70%) based on the final 30 credits of undergraduate study at BCIT or equivalent (e.g., one year of full-time studies). Option 2: alternate entry Alternate entry is for applicants who don’t have a bachelor's degree in computer science and may need to take bridging courses before being accepted to the program. Applicants are required to have the following: Post-secondary education: bachelor's degree with a minimum GPA of 3.0 out of 4.0 (73%) in another discipline based on the final 30 credits of undergraduate study, with significant knowledge of computing through formal education and/or work experience. Completed Pre-entry Assessment form [PDF] : submit the form to CompMSc@bcit.ca . The program area will review your pre-entry assessment and bridging courses may be required before applying to the program. Bridging courses will be recommended from existing COMP courses at BCIT, although transferable course work from other recognized Canadian post-secondary institutions may also be used. Applicants may be requested to send additional documents or meet with the program area. Complete the following form for submission with your online application: Mandatory Applicant Questionnaire [PDF] : This form will be used with other entrance requirements in the competitive selection for the program. Please note that two references are required on the form, and that the people listed as references must directly email their reference form to the M.Sc. admissions committee up to one week after the application deadline. Applicants who have completed post-secondary studies outside of Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia or New Zealand will require a comprehensive evaluation of their credentials by the International Credential Evaluation Service (ICES) . Credential evaluation reports from other Canadian services may be considered. Step 2: Department Review All complete applications will be reviewed by the Graduate Program Committee and ranked competitively, and applicants will be offered admission accordingly. Only complete applications with all the required supporting documentation will be evaluated for admission consideration to the program. Recommended for success Applicants with a sufficient knowledge base in computer science will be best positioned for success in this program. This may include students who have studied information and communications technology (ICT), engineering, physics, mathematics, applied sciences, or other areas where they have been exposed to computing, information technology, and programming concepts. International applicants This program is available to international applicants. Study permit: A valid BCIT study permit is required prior to starting the program. Students enrolled in the Project & Internship Path of this program must complete the mandatory work component to qualify for graduation. Post-graduation Work Permit (PGWP) eligibility : This program currently meets the PGWP eligibility requirements based on study program - graduates with a master's degree and is eligible for students to apply for a PGWP. There are no field of study requirements (CIP) for graduates with a master’s degree. Students are responsible for meeting all Immigration, Refugees, and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) PGWP eligibility requirements . Final PGWP approval is at the discretion of IRCC. Apply to program Note: The September 2026 intake is now closed for new applications. Applications for the September 2027 intake will be accepted starting October 1, 2026. To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply Go back Overview Next up Costs & Supplies

rule_sets.name: Year 2 alternative pathway
rule_sets.notes: This degree focuses on Applied Computing, which is fundamentally related to applying computing technology and computational methods to derive solutions to complex practical problems. Course work will emphasize current issues in industry, case studies, and applied research projects. This program offers you a chance to work with an interdisciplinary and diverse team of academic supervisors that may include faculty from Computing, faculty from an application domain, as well as industry practitioners. You’ll also have the opportunity to undertake directed studies with a supervisor in a different department to explore a specific application area. For more information about faculty, visit the Faculty, Advisors & Staff page. Applied research is fundamental to the program. Two paths are offered, diverging in second year: Thesis Path – Path 1: complete a thesis project and defend it in your second year. You’ll need to demonstrate originality in the application of your knowledge, either through new publishable research, or a novel solution to an existing practical problem. This is the best path if you’re interested in possibly pursuing a future Ph.D. Project & Internship Path – Path 2: a one-semester research project with a one-semester internship, which may be paid or unpaid. The internship will involve an external company or a BCIT lab where you can learn how advanced computing techniques are applied to solve interdisciplinary problems. The research project may be done in collaboration with the sponsor from the internship, providing added value in terms of practical utility. Students will also complete a 3-credit special topics course, covering emerging areas in Applied Computing, such as Quantum Computing, Generative AI, or Deep Learning. Both paths will require students to: examine literature in a related discipline, recognize gaps and limitations in existing technologies and processes, organize and plan their approach, and demonstrate competence in applying advanced techniques to solve problems. In both paths, students will present a written argument that addresses a complex problem in applied computing. Did you miss our Info Session? Grading Students will be required to maintain a minimum average of 70% across all courses in the program before starting their thesis or research project. Student progress through the program will be monitored by the supervisor, in consultation with the Program Head. Program delivery In person: This program is delivered on campus. program.program_overview: The Master of Science Degree in Applied Computing gives you in-depth computing knowledge to solve complex real-world problems across industries and sectors. Through an interdisciplinary and rigorous full-time curriculum, you’ll be equipped to provide technical leadership in a professional setting or pursue further academic study. Note: The September 2026 intake is now closed for new applications. Applications for the September 2027 intake will be accepted starting October 1, 2026. Delivery: in person. See details . BCIT Master of Science in Applied Computing About the program Applied computing integrates information technology, computer science, and industry. You’ll take courses in core computing, and you will have the opportunity to work in an application area in another discipline. You’ll develop a deep understanding of how advanced computing, tools, and computational methods can be applied in practice to overcome challenges and create efficiencies. The program employs a cohort model, with the same group in all courses. This allows you to work through the program together, sharing your experience and expertise and building industry connections that will last long after you graduate 1 intake: September 4 15-week terms, normally completed over two academic years full time First year with two terms , delivered in-person, including: Algorithm analysis Human-centered Computing Machine Learning (ML) & Artificial Intelligence (AI) Data Science Cybersecurity Research methods Second year on thesis path or internship & project path Based on BCIT Burnaby Campus, and possibly the Downtown Campus or field locations where appropriate. You’ll be uniquely qualified to apply your knowledge and skills in various areas, such as: computational science rehabilitation engineering building science biotechnology autonomous vehicles sustainability smart micro-grids social impacts of technology network security an approved project area of your choosing based on your professional background See the Program Details to learn more. Who it’s for This degree might be for you if you: Are inspired to maximize the societal benefit of computing by solving real-world issues Would like to apply your skills in industry after graduation, but might also consider applying for a PhD Are looking for a cohort-based program where you’ll work with other students to share problem-solving skills and approaches, as you would in a work setting Have an applied problem you believe could be improved through computing Would like to study with computing faculty, application experts outside of computing, and industry partners Students will also have the opportunity to undertake directed studies with a supervisor in a different department to gain additional knowledge in a specific application area. Please review the Entrance Requirements to learn more. What grads can do Provide technical leadership for software/system development teams Demonstrate deep, critical knowledge and understanding of advanced topics in computing science Analyze how computing systems and software can be used in practical applications and interdisciplinary fields Design, develop, and implement innovative solutions to industry problems with consideration to relevant ethical, social and environmental issues Explain and advocate for applied computing solutions to specialist and non-specialist audiences in both business and academic settings See the Graduating & Jobs page to learn more. rule_sets.name: Applied Computing MSc competitive admission
rule_sets.notes: Applicants currently in the final term of their degree program must be on track to graduate by July prior to the start of the intake and may be conditionally accepted based on successful completion of their degree. Scheduled intakes September each year. Application processing Applications are accepted: First round: October 1st* to January 31st* Second round: February 1st* to March 31st* Third round: April 1st* to June 15th* International applicants must hold a valid BCIT study permit to apply to the third round. *or next business day Indigenous applicants: Read about Indigenous student support available for BCIT Computing programs. Entrance requirements Competitive entry: Two-step process Admission to the program is competitive, with preference given to applicants with a combination of: Academic grades above the minimum Relevant industry experience Step 1: Meet the following entrance requirements: English language proficiency: Graduate Studies – English Studies 12 (67%) or equivalent One of the following entry requirements: Option 1: standard entry Post-secondary education: A bachelor’s degree in computer science or equivalent, such as BCIT’s Bachelor of Science in Applied Computer Science , with a minimum GPA of 2.8 out of 4.0 (70%) based on the final 30 credits of undergraduate study at BCIT or equivalent (e.g., one year of full-time studies). Option 2: alternate entry Alternate entry is for applicants who don’t have a bachelor's degree in computer science and may need to take bridging courses before being accepted to the program. Applicants are required to have the following: Post-secondary education: bachelor's degree with a minimum GPA of 3.0 out of 4.0 (73%) in another discipline based on the final 30 credits of undergraduate study, with significant knowledge of computing through formal education and/or work experience. Completed Pre-entry Assessment form [PDF] : submit the form to CompMSc@bcit.ca . The program area will review your pre-entry assessment and bridging courses may be required before applying to the program. Bridging courses will be recommended from existing COMP courses at BCIT, although transferable course work from other recognized Canadian post-secondary institutions may also be used. Applicants may be requested to send additional documents or meet with the program area. Complete the following form for submission with your online application: Mandatory Applicant Questionnaire [PDF] : This form will be used with other entrance requirements in the competitive selection for the program. Please note that two references are required on the form, and that the people listed as references must directly email their reference form to the M.Sc. admissions committee up to one week after the application deadline. Applicants who have completed post-secondary studies outside of Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia or New Zealand will require a comprehensive evaluation of their credentials by the International Credential Evaluation Service (ICES) . Credential evaluation reports from other Canadian services may be considered. Step 2: Department Review All complete applications will be reviewed by the Graduate Program Committee and ranked competitively, and applicants will be offered admission accordingly. Only complete applications with all the required supporting documentation will be evaluated for admission consideration to the program. Recommended for success Applicants with a sufficient knowledge base in computer science will be best positioned for success in this program. This may include students who have studied information and communications technology (ICT), engineering, physics, mathematics, applied sciences, or other areas where they have been exposed to computing, information technology, and programming concepts. International applicants This program is available to international applicants. Study permit: A valid BCIT study permit is required prior to starting the program. Students enrolled in the Project & Internship Path of this program must complete the mandatory work component to qualify for graduation. Post-graduation Work Permit (PGWP) eligibility : This program currently meets the PGWP eligibility requirements based on study program - graduates with a master's degree and is eligible for students to apply for a PGWP. There are no field of study requirements (CIP) for graduates with a master’s degree. Students are responsible for meeting all Immigration, Refugees, and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) PGWP eligibility requirements . Final PGWP approval is at the discretion of IRCC. Apply to program Note: The September 2026 intake is now closed for new applications. Applications for the September 2027 intake will be accepted starting October 1, 2026. To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply Go back Overview Next up Costs & Supplies

rule_sets.name: Year 2 alternative pathway
rule_sets.notes: This degree focuses on Applied Computing, which is fundamentally related to applying computing technology and computational methods to derive solutions to complex practical problems. Course work will emphasize current issues in industry, case studies, and applied research projects. This program offers you a chance to work with an interdisciplinary and diverse team of academic supervisors that may include faculty from Computing, faculty from an application domain, as well as industry practitioners. You’ll also have the opportunity to undertake directed studies with a supervisor in a different department to explore a specific application area. For more information about faculty, visit the Faculty, Advisors & Staff page. Applied research is fundamental to the program. Two paths are offered, diverging in second year: Thesis Path – Path 1: complete a thesis project and defend it in your second year. You’ll need to demonstrate originality in the application of your knowledge, either through new publishable research, or a novel solution to an existing practical problem. This is the best path if you’re interested in possibly pursuing a future Ph.D. Project & Internship Path – Path 2: a one-semester research project with a one-semester internship, which may be paid or unpaid. The internship will involve an external company or a BCIT lab where you can learn how advanced computing techniques are applied to solve interdisciplinary problems. The research project may be done in collaboration with the sponsor from the internship, providing added value in terms of practical utility. Students will also complete a 3-credit special topics course, covering emerging areas in Applied Computing, such as Quantum Computing, Generative AI, or Deep Learning. Both paths will require students to: examine literature in a related discipline, recognize gaps and limitations in existing technologies and processes, organize and plan their approach, and demonstrate competence in applying advanced techniques to solve problems. In both paths, students will present a written argument that addresses a complex problem in applied computing. Did you miss our Info Session? Please see the recording from October 2024: BCIT Master of Science in Applied Computing | Info Session Program length Two years, full-time. The maximum time to complete this program is five years. Grading Students will be required to maintain a minimum average of 70% across all courses in the program before starting their thesis or research project. Student progress through the program will be monitored by the supervisor, in consultation with the Program Head. Program delivery In person: This program is delivered on campus. Program location Burnaby Campus 3700 Willingdon Avenue Burnaby, BC Go back Courses Next up Graduating & Jobs

program.program_overview: The Master of Science Degree in Applied Computing gives you in-depth computing knowledge to solve complex real-world problems across industries and sectors. Through an interdisciplinary and rigorous full-time curriculum, you’ll be equipped to provide technical leadership in a professional setting or pursue further academic study. Note: The September 2026 intake is now closed for new applications. Applications for the September 2027 intake will be accepted starting October 1, 2026. Delivery: in person. See details . BCIT Master of Science in Applied Computing About the program Applied computing integrates information technology, computer science, and industry. You’ll take courses in core computing, and you will have the opportunity to work in an application area in another discipline. You’ll develop a deep understanding of how advanced computing, tools, and computational methods can be applied in practice to overcome challenges and create efficiencies. The program employs a cohort model, with the same group in all courses. This allows you to work through the program together, sharing your experience and expertise and building industry connections that will last long after you graduate 1 intake: September 4 15-week terms, normally completed over two academic years full time First year with two terms , delivered in-person, including: Algorithm analysis Human-centered Computing Machine Learning (ML) & Artificial Intelligence (AI) Data Science Cybersecurity Research methods Second year on thesis path or internship & project path Based on BCIT Burnaby Campus, and possibly the Downtown Campus or field locations where appropriate. You’ll be uniquely qualified to apply your knowledge and skills in various areas, such as: computational science rehabilitation engineering building science biotechnology autonomous vehicles sustainability smart micro-grids social impacts of technology network security an approved project area of your choosing based on your professional background See the Program Details to learn more. Who it’s for This degree might be for you if you: Are inspired to maximize the societal benefit of computing by solving real-world issues Would like to apply your skills in industry after graduation, but might also consider applying for a PhD Are looking for a cohort-based program where you’ll work with other students to share problem-solving skills and approaches, as you would in a work setting Have an applied problem you believe could be improved through computing Would like to study with computing faculty, application experts outside of computing, and industry partners Students will also have the opportunity to undertake directed studies with a supervisor in a different department to gain additional knowledge in a specific application area. Please review the Entrance Requirements to learn more. What grads can do Provide technical leadership for software/system development teams Demonstrate deep, critical knowledge and understanding of advanced topics in computing science Analyze how computing systems and software can be used in practical applications and interdisciplinary fields Design, develop, and implement innovative solutions to industry problems with consideration to relevant ethical, social and environmental issues Explain and advocate for applied computing solutions to specialist and non-specialist audiences in both business and academic settings See the Graduating & Jobs page to learn more. Next up Entrance Requirements

content.text:
No. **The Applied Computing — Master of Science program cannot guarantee you a job after graduation.**

It is designed to prepare graduates for technical leadership and applied computing roles. The **Project & Internship Path** includes **COMP 9400 — Industry Internship**, but the internship may be paid or unpaid and does not guarantee permanent employment.

Your job prospects will depend on factors such as your skills, experience, portfolio, networking, and the job market.

[Official program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/applied-computing-master-of-science-full-time-m600msc/)

expectation.question: What about its admission requirements?

response.answer:
For the **Construction Management — Bachelor of Technology** program, admission requires:

### Requirements for everyone
- An approved **departmental pre-entry assessment** completed before applying.
- **English Studies 12 with at least 73%**, or an equivalent.
- **Exactly one** of the following entry pathways:

### Entry pathways

**Pathway A — Construction-related credential**
- A recognized construction-related diploma or degree with at least **67% GPA**.
- At least **1 year of construction-industry work experience**.

**Pathway B — Unrelated credential plus bridging certificate**
- An unrelated diploma or degree from a recognized institution with at least **67% GPA**.
- A **BCIT Construction Operations Associate Certificate** with at least **67% GPA**.
- At least **1 year of construction-industry work experience**.

**Pathway C — Extensive construction-management experience**
- An unrelated diploma or degree from a recognized institution with at least **67% GPA**.
- At least **8 years of North American construction-management experience** in mid- or senior-level roles.

**Pathway D — Red Seal trade**
- An approved Red Seal trade, such as carpenter, electrician, plumber, welder level A, or another listed trade.
- One accepted math option at **60%**, such as Pre-Calculus 11, Foundations Math 11, Workplace Math 11, or an accepted equivalent.
- A Construction Operations Associate Certificate with at least **67% GPA**.
- At least **1 year of construction-industry experience**, in addition to apprenticeship hours.

For specified international post-secondary credentials obtained outside **Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, or New Zealand**, an accepted comprehensive credential evaluation is required, including course-by-course evaluation and GPA calculation. A master’s degree alone is not sufficient for admission.

The program is listed as available to international applicants, but the available data does not publish a study-permit determination. Please confirm current application details with BCIT.

[Program details and source](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/construction-management-bachelor-of-technology-full-time-part-time-8800btech/)

For more information, see BCIT Admissions: https://www.bcit.ca/admission/.

content.text:
For the **Construction Management — Bachelor of Technology** program, admission requires:

### Requirements for everyone
- An approved **departmental pre-entry assessment** completed before applying.
- **English Studies 12 with at least 73%**, or an equivalent.
- **Exactly one** of the following entry pathways:

### Entry pathways

**Pathway A — Construction-related credential**
- A recognized construction-related diploma or degree with at least **67% GPA**.
- At least **1 year of construction-industry work experience**.

**Pathway B — Unrelated credential plus bridging certificate**
- An unrelated diploma or degree from a recognized institution with at least **67% GPA**.
- A **BCIT Construction Operations Associate Certificate** with at least **67% GPA**.
- At least **1 year of construction-industry work experience**.

**Pathway C — Extensive construction-management experience**
- An unrelated diploma or degree from a recognized institution with at least **67% GPA**.
- At least **8 years of North American construction-management experience** in mid- or senior-level roles.

**Pathway D — Red Seal trade**
- An approved Red Seal trade, such as carpenter, electrician, plumber, welder level A, or another listed trade.
- One accepted math option at **60%**, such as Pre-Calculus 11, Foundations Math 11, Workplace Math 11, or an accepted equivalent.
- A Construction Operations Associate Certificate with at least **67% GPA**.
- At least **1 year of construction-industry experience**, in addition to apprenticeship hours.

For specified international post-secondary credentials obtained outside **Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, or New Zealand**, an accepted comprehensive credential evaluation is required, including course-by-course evaluation and GPA calculation. A master’s degree alone is not sufficient for admission.

The program is listed as available to international applicants, but the available data does not publish a study-permit determination. Please confirm current application details with BCIT.

[Program details and source](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/construction-management-bachelor-of-technology-full-time-part-time-8800btech/)

content.text:
You’re referring to **Construction Management — Bachelor of Technology**.

- **Credential:** Bachelor of Technology / Bachelor’s Degree  
- **Format:** Full-time or part-time  
- **Delivery:** In person  
- **Campus:** Burnaby  
- **School:** School of Construction and the Environment  
- **Overview:** A degree-completion program developing construction-project management, technical, and interpersonal skills.

### Curriculum areas

The program includes:

- **Construction Controls and Techniques**, including:
  - **CMGT 7190 — Construction Planning and Controls**
  - **CMGT 7190 — Construction Planning and Controls**
  - The available record does not provide display course codes for the other courses in this component.
- **Organization Management**, including:
  - **BUSA 7250 — Management Skills and Applications**
  - **CMGT 7330 — Finance for Construction Managers**
  - **CMGT 7420 — Construction Law** *(display code available in the record: not provided)*
  - **CMGT 8435 — Construction Enterprise Management** *(display code available in the record: not provided)*
- **Stakeholder Engagement**, including:
  - **CMGT 7535 — Leadership and Interpersonal Skills**
  - **CMGT 7660 — Environmental Considerations in Construction** *(display code available in the record: not provided)*
  - **CMGT 8602 — Engagement of Project Stakeholders** *(display code available in the record: not provided)*
- **Management electives:** Complete at least **4 credits from the approved management elective pool**. This is credit-based, not a fixed number of courses.
- **Liberal Studies:** Complete at least **12 credits**, including:
  - **LIBS 7001 — Critical Reading and Writing**
  - **LIBS 7002 — Applied Ethics**
  - **LIBS 7013 — Race, Class and Gender: Intersections**
- **Professional Standards**, including:
  - **CMGT 7810 — Advanced Industry Communication** *(display code available in the record: not provided)*
  - **CMGT 8211 — Industry Collaborations** *(display code available in the record: not provided)*
  - **CMGT 8700 — Industry Based Project Proposal**
  - Then choose **one** final-project option:
    - **CMGT 8800 — Industry Based Project**
    - **CMGT 8810 — Industry Based Project**

For part-time study, **LIBS 7013 — Race, Class and Gender: Intersections** may be replaced by **3 additional approved Liberal Studies elective credits**; the other Liberal Studies requirements remain.

[Program details and curriculum](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/construction-management-bachelor-of-technology-full-time-part-time-8800btech/)

What about its admission requirements?

For the **Construction Management — Bachelor of Technology** program, admission requires:

### Requirements for everyone
- An approved **departmental pre-entry assessment** completed before applying.
- **English Studies 12 with at least 73%**, or an equivalent.
- **Exactly one** of the following entry pathways:

### Entry pathways

**Pathway A — Construction-related credential**
- A recognized construction-related diploma or degree with at least **67% GPA**.
- At least **1 year of construction-industry work experience**.

**Pathway B — Unrelated credential plus bridging certificate**
- An unrelated diploma or degree from a recognized institution with at least **67% GPA**.
- A **BCIT Construction Operations Associate Certificate** with at least **67% GPA**.
- At least **1 year of construction-industry work experience**.

**Pathway C — Extensive construction-management experience**
- An unrelated diploma or degree from a recognized institution with at least **67% GPA**.
- At least **8 years of North American construction-management experience** in mid- or senior-level roles.

**Pathway D — Red Seal trade**
- An approved Red Seal trade, such as carpenter, electrician, plumber, welder level A, or another listed trade.
- One accepted math option at **60%**, such as Pre-Calculus 11, Foundations Math 11, Workplace Math 11, or an accepted equivalent.
- A Construction Operations Associate Certificate with at least **67% GPA**.
- At least **1 year of construction-industry experience**, in addition to apprenticeship hours.

For specified international post-secondary credentials obtained outside **Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, or New Zealand**, an accepted comprehensive credential evaluation is required, including course-by-course evaluation and GPA calculation.
